subject: Dedicated capacity — tail-burst & commitment clarifications
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@edgeworks.ai>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@edgeworks.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick: Dedicated plan sizing — tail bursts and commit questions

Hi Hiro,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency figures. We're starting to map out a committed reserved fleet plan and I have a couple of items we'd like your help making concrete before we commit. High level: we have very spiky traffic (large tail bursts during promotional windows), mixed prompt types (few-shot chat + retrieval-augmented snippets), and variable response lengths.

Questions:
- What data points do you need from us to size a dedicated pool that handles 10x day-over-day baseline spikes for <2 hour windows without impacting p95 latency?
- How do you model tail-burst costs vs steady-state commit? Any recommended fallback/oversubscription approach to limit committed GPU footprint?

I attached a small telemetry sample from last month's campaign (anonymized). Let me know if you need a longer extract.

Best,
Lena
Head of Platform
EdgeWorks

[Attachment: edgeworks-telemetry-sample.csv (CSV, 52KB)]

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@edgeworks.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: Dedicated plan sizing — tail bursts and commit questions

Hi Lena — thanks for the sample and the clear summary. Short answers up front: we can size for bursts, but the economics and recommended architecture depend on three profile dimensions: concurrency distribution, prompt/response token mix, and session duration (KV cache behavior). To give you a fast, actionable estimate we need:

1) Token-level distribution: average prompt tokens, average response tokens, and 99th percentile response tokens (typical promo responses often have long tails).
2) Concurrency patterns: baseline active sessions, burst peak active sessions (and whether burst is single big spike or many smaller parallel spikes).
3) Session semantics: are KV caches re-used across requests (session affinity) or are most requests stateless?
4) SLA tolerance: p50/p95/p99 latency targets and which you want guaranteed under commit.

I uploaded a short intake we use for this exercise and pasted a compact questionnaire below — if you can fill the fields, we will run a quick occupancy and cost model and propose a committed footprint + a recommended oversubscription and burst buffer.

Quick questionnaire (paste answers inline or attach a CSV) —
- Baseline RPS and Burst peak RPS (avg and peak windows)
- Avg prompt tokens / median response tokens / p99 response tokens
- Ratio of chat-style sessions vs short generation API (percent)
- Typical session length (seconds) and fraction with KV cache reuse
- Target p95 latency (ms) under committed capacity
- Any blackout windows / promotional cadence (dates + typical duration)

Next steps: once we have this, Marissa (solutions) will run a traffic-slice simulation and propose a recommended GPU mix and a fallback routing policy for overflow traffic. Can we target a 48-hour turnaround if you can send the answers today?

Cheers,
Hiro
VP Pre-Sales, Redwood Inference

[Attachment referenced: dedicated-sizing-intake.md (template)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@edgeworks.ai>
Cc: Hiro Tanaka <hiro@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 12:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: Dedicated plan sizing — tail bursts and commit questions

Hi Lena — Marissa here (solutions engineering). I took a quick pass through the telemetry extract and added inline questions where the sample lacked clarity. I'll run a synthetic stress test once you provide the numeric answers below.

Inline notes from CSV:
- The sample shows clear dayparting with a ~9x peak vs baseline across a 90–120 minute window on promo days. We'll model both a single-node burst (many concurrent requests to a small pool) and a multi-node burst (wide fanout).

Questions / fields to fill:
1) Baseline RPS: __45__ (fill if different)
2) Burst peak RPS (5-min peak): __405__
3) Avg prompt tokens: __42__
4) Median response tokens: __130__
5) p99 response tokens: __1,240__
6) Percent chat-style sessions: __35%__
7) Typical session length: __18s__
8) Percent sessions with KV reuse: __62%__
9) Target p95 latency under commit: __350ms__

Notes / assumptions we'll test:
- With those inputs, initial analysis suggests an occupancy of ~0.28 GPUs per 1k steady-state RPS for our 80B quantized profile; tail bursts inflate token compute cost (and KV cache reuse reduces per-token cost for chat flows).
- Recommended approach: commit to steady-state fleet sized for 2x baseline with a dedicated burst buffer (either a small hot pool of faster SKUs or an autoscale burst through dedicated burst credits).

Deliverables if you confirm:
- Simulated p95/p99 latencies for both single-node and multi-node burst shapes
- GPU SKU mix (quantized 80B vs 40B fallbacks), occupancy table, and monthly commit suggestion with burst reserve sizing
- Suggested fallback policy (drop to cheaper 40B quantized models at p99 pressure and route overflow to hosted spare capacity)

I'll schedule a 60-minute sizing workshop if that helps — Hiro, can you confirm availability tomorrow afternoon? Lena, if you fill the 9 fields above and attach a 24-hour RPS histogram (CSV), we'll run the sims and share a short slide with proposed commit plus cost delta.

— Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
